summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (Section 4 of the paper).

Pipeline (Section 4.5 summary):
  1. Bin Center Selection: equal-frequency bin centers from observed values
     only, at evenly-spaced percentiles (Eq. 4).
  2. Proximity Assignment: each observed value -> nearest bin center (Eq. 5).
  3. One-Hot Encoding: binary encoding of observed features (Eqs. 6-7).
  4. Missing Value Handling: three-level cascading fallback using kernel mean
     embedding -- intersection matching (Eqs. 8-10), union matching
     (Eqs. 11-12), global prior (Eqs. 13-14).

The representation z_i in [0,1]^(d*nbins) defines the proximity kernel
K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n (Eq. 15).
"""

import numpy as np


def fit_bins(X, nbins):
    """Eq. (4): c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)), k = 1..nbins.

    Uses observed values only. Percentiles are linearly interpolated (A2).
    Returns centers of shape (d, nbins); NaN rows mark entirely-missing
    features, for which a uniform prior is used downstream (A7).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    qs = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)  # (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) for k = 1..nbins
    centers = np.full((d, nbins), np.nan)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            continue  # entirely missing feature -> uniform prior (A7)
        centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, qs, method="linear")
    return centers


def assign_bins(X, centers):
    """Eq. (5): b_{i,j} = argmin_k |x_{i,j} - c_{j,k}| for observed values.

    Ties break to the lowest bin index via np.argmin (A3). Missing entries
    (NaN value, or entirely-missing feature) get bin index -1.
    Returns integer array B of shape (n, d).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    nbins = centers.shape[1]
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=np.int64)
    for j in range(d):
        cj = centers[j]
        if np.isnan(cj).any():
            continue
        col = X[:, j]
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(col)
        if not obs_mask.any():
            continue
        dist = np.abs(col[obs_mask, None] - cj[None, :])
        B[obs_mask, j] = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)
    return B


def encode_observed(B, nbins):
    """Eqs. (6)-(7): one-hot encode observed bin assignments.

    Returns H of shape (n, d, nbins); missing entries are all-zero rows.
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=np.float64)
    ii, jj = np.nonzero(B >= 0)
    H[ii, jj, B[ii, jj]] = 1.0
    return H


def compute_priors(B, nbins):
    """Eq. (13): p_{j,k} = (# observed samples of feature j in bin k) / (# observed).

    Uniform 1/nbins when a feature has no observed values (A7).
    Returns priors of shape (d, nbins).
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    priors = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins, dtype=np.float64)
    for j in range(d):
        bj = B[:, j]
        obs = bj >= 0
        if not obs.any():
            continue
        counts = np.bincount(bj[obs], minlength=nbins).astype(np.float64)
        priors[j] = counts / counts.sum()
    return priors


def compute_fallback_encodings(B, H, priors):
    """Three-level cascading fallback (Section 4.2). Fills H in place.

    For each missing entry (i, j), with O_i the observed features of sample i:
      Level 1 (Eqs. 8-10): S1(i) = samples m != i whose bins match sample i on
        ALL features in O_i. Estimate h_{i,j} as the mean one-hot vector over
        the m in S1(i) that have feature j observed (A8).
      Level 2 (Eqs. 11-12): S2(i) = samples m != i matching sample i on ANY
        feature in O_i. Same mean-embedding estimate over observed-at-j members.
      Level 3 (Eqs. 13-14): global prior distribution of feature j.
    A sample with no observed features at all falls back to the global prior
    for every missing feature (equivalent to a vacuous match).
    Returns dict with per-level counts and per-sample level labels.
    """
    n, d, nbins = H.shape
    level_counts = {1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0}
    levels = np.full((n, d), 0, dtype=np.int64)  # level used per entry (0 = observed)
    for i in range(n):
        O_i = np.nonzero(B[i] >= 0)[0]
        M_i = np.nonzero(B[i] < 0)[0]
        if M_i.size == 0:
            continue
        if O_i.size == 0:
            for j in M_i:
                H[i, j] = priors[j]
                level_counts[3] += 1
                levels[i, j] = 3
            continue
        # eq[m, t] is True iff sample m matches sample i on O_i[t]; samples with
        # a missing bin (-1) never match an observed bin (>= 0), matching the
        # definition C_{i,j} = {m : m != i, b_{m,j} = b_{i,j}} (Eq. 8).
        eq = B[:, O_i] == B[i, O_i]
        s1_mask = eq.all(axis=1)
        s1_mask[i] = False
        S1 = np.nonzero(s1_mask)[0]
        s2_mask = eq.any(axis=1)
        s2_mask[i] = False
        S2 = np.nonzero(s2_mask)[0]
        for j in M_i:
            if S1.size:
                m1 = S1[B[S1, j] >= 0]
                if m1.size:

            level_counts[3] += 1
            levels[i, j] = 3
    return {"level_counts": level_counts, "levels": levels}


def build_representation(X, nbins):
    """Build the kernel representation Z of shape (n, d*nbins).

    Returns (Z, diagnostics) where diagnostics includes the bin assignments,
    centers, priors, fallback level counts and the reshaped encoding H.

    n, d = X.shape
    centers = fit_bins(X, nbins)

"""Clustering evaluation: K-means on the kernel representation + NMI.

Protocol (Section 5.1): K-means with the number of clusters set to the
ground-truth number of classes; each experiment repeated 10 times and the
average NMI reported. For the proximity kernel we search nbins in
{2, 3, 4, 6, 8} and report the best mean NMI per dataset (A9).

K-means in the representation space Z is the kernel-based clustering the
paper describes around Eq. (19); sklearn KMeans with k-means++ init and
n_init=10 is the standard default (A4). NMI is sklearn's
normalized_mutual_info_score with its default arithmetic averaging (A5).
"""

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation


def evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds, n_init=10):
    """Run KMeans(n_clusters=K) on Z once per seed; return (mean, std, per-seed)."""
    nmis = []
    for seed in seeds:
        km = KMeans(
            n_clusters=K, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=int(seed)
        )
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        nmis.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    return float(np.mean(nmis)), float(np.std(nmis)), nmis


def search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds, n_init=10, verbose=True):
    """Evaluate every nbins in the grid; select the one with highest mean NMI."""
    d = X.shape[1]
    results = {}
    for nb in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nb)
        mean, std, per_seed = evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds, n_init=n_init)
        results[int(nb)] = {
            "mean_nmi": mean,
            "std_nmi": std,
            "per_seed_nmi": per_seed,
            "z_shape": list(Z.shape),
            "diagnostics": {
                "n_missing_entries": diag["n_missing_entries"],
                "level_counts": diag["level_counts"],
            },
        }
        if verbose:
            print(
                f"[search] nbins={nb}: mean NMI={mean:.4f} +/- {std:.4f} "
                f"(fallback levels {diag['level_counts']})"
            )
    best_nbins = max(results, key=lambda k: results[k]["mean_nmi"])
    return best_nbins, results

def check_representation(Z, diag, d, label=""):
    """Validate the representation and kernel; returns a dict of check results."""
    n = Z.shape[0]
    nbins = diag["nbins"]
    H = diag["H"]
    B = diag["B"]
    checks = {}
    checks["z_shape_ok"] = list(Z.shape) == [n, d * nbins]
    checks["z_finite"] = bool(np.isfinite(Z).all())
    # R14 / one-hot validity: every per-feature encoding sums to exactly 1
    # (one-hot for observed, probability distribution for missing).
    h_sums = H.sum(axis=2)
    checks["encoding_sums_to_one"] = bool(np.allclose(h_sums, 1.0))
    # complete rows have exactly d ones (R14)
    complete_rows = (B >= 0).all(axis=1)
    if complete_rows.any():
        zc = Z[complete_rows]
        checks["complete_rows_exactly_d_ones"] = bool(
            np.allclose(zc.sum(axis=1), d) and np.isin(zc, [0.0, 1.0]).all()
        )
    else:
        checks["complete_rows_exactly_d_ones"] = "no complete rows"
    # bin indices valid
    bvals = B[B >= 0]
    checks["bin_indices_in_range"] = bool(
        bvals.size == 0 or (bvals.min() >= 0 and bvals.max() <= nbins - 1)
    )
    # kernel validity: symmetric, PSD (via eigenvalues), entries in [0, 1]
    K = proximity_kernel(Z, d)
    checks["kernel_symmetric"] = bool(np.allclose(K, K.T))
    checks["kernel_diag_le_1"] = bool((np.diag(K) <= 1.0 + 1e-12).all())
    checks["kernel_in_01"] = bool(K.min() >= -1e-12 and K.max() <= 1.0 + 1e-12)
    eig = np.linalg.eigvalsh(K)
    checks["kernel_psd_min_eig"] = float(eig.min())
    checks["kernel_psd"] = bool(eig.min() >= -1e-10)
    checks["n_missing_entries"] = diag["n_missing_entries"]
    checks["fallback_level_counts"] = diag["level_counts"]
    bad = [k for k, v in checks.items() if isinstance(v, bool) and not v]
    status = "OK" if not bad else f"FAILED: {bad}"
    print(f"[checks:{label}] {status}")
    for k, v in checks.items():
        print(f"    {k}: {v}")
    return checks

audit_summary: The match target C1 is faithfully reproduced: UCI Hepatitis (155x19, 2 classes, 167 missing '?' entries), full transductive K-means with K=2, NMI, 10 seeds, and nbins searched over {2,3,4,6,8}. The clean rerun computes NMI 0.2289091446, essentially identical to the paper's 0.2289 (abs diff 9.1e-06). The 0.2289 constant in reproduce.py is used only for the pass/fail target_check and does not enter the computed metric; the value is derived from data. Most method requirements are implemented, with the main caveat that the fallback matching is brute-force O(n^2 d) rather than the paper's claimed linear-time procedure, which is immaterial at n=155. Claims C2-C8 were not attempted, but they are not the match target and the target run itself was not scaled down. No wrong dataset, split, metric, method substitution, or hardcoded result was found.

requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins masks observed values per feature (~np.isnan) and computes np.percentile only on those; missing values never enter bin centers.
fit_bins uses np.linspace(0, 100, nbins) with linear interpolation, matching Eq. (4)'s evenly spaced percentiles including min/max (A2).
assign_bins computes absolute distances to each feature's centers and uses np.argmin, breaking ties to the lowest bin index (A3).
encode_observed builds H[n, d, nbins] one-hot rows for observed bin assignments, and build_representation flattens H to Z.
compute_fallback_encodings implements S1 intersection, then S2 union, then global prior, and reports per-level counts (61/106/0 on Hepatitis).
Level 1 uses eq.all over observed features O_i, excludes self, and averages H[:, j] over S1 members with feature j observed (A8).
Level 2 uses eq.any over O_i, excludes self, and averages over union-matching members observed at j; 106 entries used this level.
Level 3 uses compute_priors, i.e. observed bin frequencies per feature, with uniform fallback for entirely missing features (A7); implemented though not triggered on Hepatitis.
proximity_kernel returns (Z @ Z.T) / d. Clustering is run on Z; for this linear kernel that is equivalent to kernel K-means with K, since the 1/d constant cancels.
Evaluation uses sklearn KMeans with n_clusters=K=2 ground-truth classes and normalized_mutual_info_score on the resulting labels.
SEEDS = list(range(10)); evaluate_nbins averages NMI over 10 KMeans runs and reports per-seed values.
NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]; search_nbins evaluates each and selects the best mean NMI, here nbins=2.

Binning and assignment are near O(nd log n + nd*nbins), but the fallback recomputes all-sample matches for each sample, i.e. O(n^2 d) worst case, so the paper's O(nd + d n log n) linear-time claim is not realized by this implementation. This does not affect the n=155 target value.
check_representation verifies per-feature encodings sum to 1 and complete rows have exactly d ones; the clean rerun reports complete_rows_exactly_d_ones = True.
